title: Make Scenario Version Control: Save, History, Recovery
summary: Make scenario version control lets you track changes and restore previous versions. You can compare versions to identify which modifications were made.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Because several open questions turn on staleness too, each answer says whether Make's pages settle it or stay silent.


Is Make scenario version control available on every plan? Make's toolbar and version control page states the feature is available on all plans.


Check your organization's plan against Make's pricing page and the feature's help page before building a review process around it. If the feature is missing on your plan, your change log is still the dated note.


Does Activepieces support Make scenario versions natively? No native support is documented on Make's pages. Connecting the two today means general building blocks: webhooks and HTTP requests on each side.


**Activepieces allows unlimited flows on every plan** , including free, so a custom flow for this doesn't count against a flow limit.


You would be moving data you already have access to, not reading version history through a dedicated integration, so treat any such flow as custom work you maintain.


### Can an AI step read a Make scenario's history?


Make's pages don't say. They don't describe version history as something an AI step can query, and they don't say whether AI-assisted edits are labeled as such in that history.


Until they do, assume attribution shows the account that saved the change, not whether a person or an assistant wrote it. Record that distinction in your own change note.


Where should I check for updates to this feature? Start with Make's help center page for scenario versions, then its product release notes and pricing page.


Those are the places where plan availability, restore behavior and attribution would be stated first. Date what you find, because that record goes stale like any other.
